title_en: Zou Quanbao — case of intentional destruction of property

full_text_en:
Zou Quanbao — Intentional Destruction of Property Case

Prosecutorial Authority: People's Procuratorate of Dingzhou City, Hebei Province.

Defendant: Zou Quanbao, male, 40 years old, farmer of Gedatou Village, Zhoucun Township, Dingzhou City, Hebei Province. Arrested on July 9, 1999.

The People's Procuratorate of Dingzhou City, Hebei Province filed a public prosecution with the Dingzhou City People's Court, alleging that the defendant Zou Quanbao, at approximately 5:00 p.m. on April 11, 1999, after drinking alcohol, broke into the village committee office in his village, smashed window panes, and damaged loudspeakers, telephones, currency detectors, and other items, causing economic losses of RMB 2,012 to the village committee. His conduct violated Article 275 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and constituted the crime of intentional destruction of public or private property, and the court was requested to render a judgment according to law.

The defendant Zou Quanbao argued: "It is true that I smashed up the village committee office, but I did not damage that many things."

The Dingzhou City People's Court found through trial that: In April 1993, the defendant Zou Quanbao was involved in a payment default dispute arising from a sales contract with another party. Through mediation by the Ninghe County People's Court of Tianjin, Zou Quanbao agreed to pay the outstanding amount to the counterparty by April 30, failing which three 3-ton aluminum wine storage tanks that had been sealed by the Ninghe County People's Court would be used to offset the debt. After the mediation document from the Ninghe County People's Court was served, Zou Quanbao failed to perform. In September of the same year, upon application by the counterparty, the Ninghe County People's Court decided to enforce the judgment after issuing an enforcement notice that was not complied with. When enforcement officers arrived at Gedatou Village, Zhoucun Township, Dingzhou City, Zou Quanbao went into hiding. The enforcement officers then lawfully requested the assistance of the village committee of Gedatou Village, Zhoucun Township, in the enforcement. Village committee cadres led the enforcement officers to Zou Quanbao's distillery. In the presence of the village committee cadres, the enforcement officers removed the three sealed 3-ton aluminum wine storage tanks onto trucks and instructed the village committee cadres to inform Zou Quanbao to go to the Ninghe County People's Court to complete the relevant formalities. After Zou Quanbao returned, he blamed the village committee cadres for assisting the out-of-district court in enforcement, claiming that the property enforced far exceeded the debt he owed to the counterparty, and unreasonably demanded that the village committee compensate him for his "losses," but he did not go to the Ninghe County People's Court to file an appeal or complete the formalities. Consequently, Zou Quanbao held a grudge against the village committee, refusing to pay public grain for three consecutive years in protest, and repeatedly threatened retaliation. At approximately 5:00 p.m. on April 11, 1999, Zou Quanbao, after drinking alcohol, again broke into the village committee office, smashing 14 window panes, and damaging loudspeakers, telephones, currency detectors, aluminum kettles, iron stoves, desks and chairs in the office, and burning family planning records, causing economic losses of RMB 2,012 to the village committee.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, photographs of the damaged items at the scene, the appraisal conclusion issued by the price office, and the confession of the defendant Zou Quanbao given to the public security organ. The above evidence was cross-examined in court, is objective and truthful, and was obtained lawfully. Zou Quanbao's defense in court that he did not damage that many things lacks supporting evidence and is not accepted.

The Dingzhou City People's Court held that: The Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that parties must perform mediation documents and other legally effective legal documents that are to be enforced by the people's court. If one party refuses to perform, the counterparty may apply to the people's court for enforcement. When a people's court enforces a judgment, if the person subject to enforcement is a citizen, the work unit or the grassroots organization in the place of his residence or the location of his real property shall send a representative to participate. The Ninghe County People's Court lawfully decided to enforce the judgment with respect to the property of the defendant Zou Quanbao in Gedatou Village, Zhoucun Township, Dingzhou City, and the village committee had an obligation to assist in the enforcement. Zou Quanbao, out of dissatisfaction with his village committee for assisting the people's court in completing the enforcement work, harbored a deliberate intent to retaliate and intentionally destroyed the property of the village committee, and the circumstances were serious. His conduct violated the provisions of Article 275 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of intentional destruction of property. To uphold the dignity of the law, ensure the enforcement of effective judgments, rulings, and mediation documents of the people's court, and protect the personal and property rights of units and citizens that assist the people's court in completing enforcement work from infringement, Zou Quanbao's criminal conduct must be punished according to law. Accordingly, the Dingzhou City People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 3, 1999:

The defendant Zou Quanbao is convicted of intentional destruction of property and sentenced to six months' imprisonment.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, the defendant Zou Quanbao did not appeal, and the judgment became effective.
